response.overview: Just twenty years after the notorious Salem Witch Trials in North America, the last witchcraft trial in Ireland took place in the close-knit Ulster-Scots community of Islandmagee in 1711.  Eighteen-year-old Mary Dunbar accused eight women and one man of bewitching her with spectral presences, supernatural attacks and hauntings, which went on to spark a vicious witch hunt, landing eight women in prison and leading one man to his death.  Dr Marie Cassidy, formerly Ireland's State Pathologist, investigates this witch trial, blending cultural analysis with contemporary accounts to uncover why this witch trial was Ireland’s last.
response.title: Ireland’s Last Witch Trial
